To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

income inequality is mainly influenced by economic growth, economic development, the distribution of the labor force over sectors of production and the distribution of the income over the different sectors of production.

the factors of income growth, income redistribution, income mobility, income distribution, the structure of the labor market and the structure of the capital market have significant direct influences on income inequality, while the factors of income mobility and income distribution have significant indirect influences on income inequality.

the following factors influence income inequality in a positive way: (i) the share of income of the top 10 percent of income recipients; (ii) the share of the top 1 percent of income recipients in the top 10; (iii) the share of top income recipients in the total population; and (iv) the share of capital income in total national income.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors of income distribution and their influence on income inequality, with a focus on the indirect influences of the factors on each other.

the following questions: Which factors of income inequality have been discussed in the empirical literature? What are the hypotheses about the influences of these factors on income inequality? How do the factors influence each other?
the factors that influence the income inequality in a society, and the influence mechanisms of these factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many factors that can influence income inequality.

the empirical results of the pertinent literature are too diverse, too inconsistent and too contradictory to allow for a conclusive and definite statement about the factors of income and their influence on income inequality.

the income inequality in Germany has been caused by the following factors: the income share of capital, the wage share, the income share of self-employed, the income share in the public sector, the tax burden, the unemployment rate, the share of the population with low income and the share of the elderly in the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the factors of income distribution are complex and interact with one another in many ways.
the empirical results of the studies reviewed are very diverse, which is due to the diversity of the factors and the methods of analysis.
the factors of income distribution can be grouped into six groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the factors of income distribution are not isolated, but are closely interrelated.
the factors of income distribution discussed in the empirical literature are very diverse.
income inequality is the result of a multitude of interacting factors.
